title: OOP & class modifiers
summary: Classes, abstraction, encapsulation, inheritance, and Dart 3 library boundaries.
steps: Model a feature with classes, interfaces, and clear library boundaries.
Compare abstract, base, interface, final, and sealed classes.
Explain overriding, operator overloading, and exhaustive switches.
proof: Design a result hierarchy and explain which subclasses another library may define.

title: Mixins & reusable behavior
summary: Compose behavior with mixin, with, on, lifecycle contracts, and deliberate method resolution.
steps: Write a logging mixin with an explicit host contract.
Trace two mixins, conflicting methods, and super calls.
Test behavior and dispose listeners/controllers safely.
proof: Explain when a mixin helps and when a composed service is clearer.

title: Generics & type-safe models
summary: Reusable responses, repositories, functions, maps, and bounded type parameters.
steps: Create ApiResponse<T> and a typed repository contract.
Use a generic function and an extends bound.
Remove raw List, raw generic types, and unnecessary dynamic.
proof: Share one implementation across two model types without losing static checks.

title: Extensions & SDK helpers
summary: Small helpers for String, nullable values, BuildContext, dates, and collections.
steps: Write named extensions for a nullable string and BuildContext.
Explain static resolution and extension name conflicts.
Prefer existing SDK methods and keep business rules in services.
proof: Use small, tested helpers without hiding navigation or business side effects.

title: Typedefs & callback contracts
summary: Precise function types for validators, buttons, value changes, and async work.
steps: Define a FieldValidator typedef and a validator factory.
Use VoidCallback, ValueChanged<T>, and Future<void> Function().
Replace broad Function fields with exact signatures.
proof: Make a reusable form/button API whose invalid callbacks fail static analysis.

title: Enhanced enums
summary: Model statuses, API values, getters, methods, and explicit unknown values.
steps: Add constant fields and a constructor to an enum.
Convert API strings without silently choosing a valid-but-wrong state.
Use enum values in a dropdown and exhaustive switch.
proof: Keep labels, transport values, and behavior consistent for an app status.

title: late, lazy init & lifecycle
summary: Initialize controllers and helpers safely; represent async data with explicit state.
steps: Initialize and dispose a late final controller.
Compare eager initialization with a late initializer.
Replace risky asynchronous late fields with loading/data/error states.
proof: Explain and prevent a LateInitializationError in a real widget.

title: const & factory constructors
summary: Constant contexts, immutable objects, parsing, caching, and controlled creation.
steps: Define a const constructor and compare const and runtime calls.
Write a validating factory from JSON or a map.
Explain a singleton factory and its testing tradeoffs.
proof: Explain exactly when instances are reused and when a new object is created.

title: Records & patterns
summary: Return multiple values, destructure records, and match object fields safely.
steps: Use positional and named records as return values.
Destructure an object with named fields and shorthand patterns.
Handle success and failure variants exhaustively.
proof: Replace a fragile tuple/map with a typed record and a readable pattern.

title: Cascades & object setup
summary: Use .. and ?.. correctly and distinguish them from return-value chaining.
steps: Initialize a controller or builder with a cascade.
Use a null-shorting cascade with ?.. only at its start.
Explain the receiver and result of each operation.
proof: Refactor repeated object setup without changing its behavior.

title: Null safety & defensive state
summary: Nullable types, promotion, safe access, defaults, assertions, and loading states.
steps: Use ?, ?., ??, and ??= with explicit meaning.
Promote a checked local variable instead of scattering !.
Model absent values and asynchronous failures deliberately.
proof: Handle missing data without inventing a valid value or crashing.

title: Collections, if & for
summary: Transform, filter, aggregate, mutate, and build conditional widget lists.
steps: Use collection if/for, map, where, expand, and typed fold.
Handle empty collections and failed searches safely.
Explain lazy iterables, toList, sorting, and mutation.
proof: Build a filtered list UI and aggregate its data with predictable empty states.

title: Streams & RxDart operators
summary: Transform event streams and keep searches, subscriptions, and errors under control.
steps: Compare single-subscription and broadcast streams.
Build a debounced search with distinct values and stale-result handling.
Test errors, completion, cancellation, and subscription disposal.
proof: Demonstrate that an old response cannot replace a newer query.

title: Local databases & migrations
summary: Compare SQLite/Drift, Hive, and Isar for durable on-device data.
steps: Compare query needs, schema changes, platform support, and package maintenance.
Choose one local database and migrate populated test data.
Test app restart, interrupted writes, and backup/restore behavior.
proof: Explain your storage choice and demonstrate a safe version upgrade.

title: Widget lifecycle & mounted
summary: Understand initialization, updates, deactivation, disposal, and asynchronous work.
steps: Trace StatelessWidget and StatefulWidget lifecycles.
Use initState, didChangeDependencies, didUpdateWidget, and dispose correctly.
Cancel owned work and check mounted before using a context after await.
proof: Fix a lifecycle bug and explain who owns each resource.

title: BuildContext & widget identity
summary: Inherited dependencies, Theme, navigation, ValueKey, and GlobalKey.
steps: Trace how Theme and InheritedWidget dependencies are found.
Demonstrate state moving incorrectly in an unkeyed reordered list.
Choose a ValueKey and justify any GlobalKey usage.
proof: Reorder stateful list items without attaching state to the wrong item.

title: Internationalization & localization
summary: Localized messages, plural rules, dates, right-to-left layouts, and locale switching.
steps: Generate localized strings from ARB files.
Handle plurals, interpolation, dates, and number formats.
Test long translations, RTL layout, and locale changes.
proof: Complete a core flow in two languages without hard-coded user-facing strings.

title: Layout, paint & compositing
summary: Understand constraints, render objects, layers, rasterization, and frame cost.
steps: Trace constraints down, sizes up, and parent positioning.
Distinguish build, layout, paint, compositing, and raster work.
Inspect a slow frame and explain the renderer used on that platform.
proof: Locate whether a performance problem is in Dart/UI work or raster work.

title: Custom painting, clipping & animation
summary: Create focused custom UI with CustomPainter, ClipPath, shaders, and animation controllers.
steps: Draw and hit-test a simple CustomPainter visualization.
Compare implicit animation with an owned AnimationController.
Measure clipping/shader cost and respect reduced motion.
proof: Ship a smooth custom interaction with correct disposal and semantics.

title: Slivers & lazy lists
summary: Compose large scrollable screens without building every item at once.
steps: Build with ListView.builder and stable keys.
Compose SliverAppBar, SliverList, and SliverGrid.
Measure scrolling and preserve position across navigation.
proof: Scroll a large dataset smoothly with correct identity and pagination.

title: Provider, GetX, Riverpod & BLoC
summary: Compare state models, then build depth with one approach.
steps: Compare local state, Provider/ChangeNotifier, GetX, Riverpod, and BLoC/Cubit.
Implement loading/data/error and dependency injection in one chosen tool.
Test state transitions without coupling business logic to widgets.
proof: Explain your selected tool’s lifecycle, data flow, and testing tradeoffs.

title: Clean Architecture & SOLID
summary: Entities, use cases, repositories, and dependency direction sized to the feature.
steps: Separate domain rules from transport and widgets.
Apply SOLID to a real change without creating unnecessary layers.
Use a repository contract and a fake in a unit test.
proof: Change a data source without rewriting business rules.

title: State restoration
summary: Restore a user’s task after process death without confusing UI state with durable data.
steps: Use RestorationMixin and restoration IDs for a small flow.
Distinguish transient UI state, restorable state, and persisted domain records.
Test process destruction and restoration on a device.
proof: Recover form/navigation state without corrupting saved records.

title: Freezed & JSON code generation
summary: Generate predictable immutable models and serialization with explicit build steps.
steps: Generate a model using freezed and json_serializable.
Handle unknown/missing JSON values and evolving fields.
Make generated-code updates repeatable in CI.
proof: Regenerate a changed model and keep parsing behavior covered by tests.

title: Dependency injection & lifetimes
summary: Use constructor injection, get_it, or Riverpod to make ownership explicit.
steps: Inject an API/repository through a constructor.
Compare get_it registrations with Riverpod providers and overrides.
Test scopes, disposal, and replacement with fakes.
proof: Swap a service in tests and explain when each instance is created and disposed.

title: REST clients with Dio & Retrofit
summary: Typed requests, serialization, interceptors, cancellation, and consistent errors.
steps: Build a typed API client with Dio or Retrofit.
Handle timeouts, auth refresh, cancellation, and transport errors.
Test malformed responses and avoid unsafe automatic retries.
proof: Make a failed or expired-token request recover predictably.

title: GraphQL, Ferry & Artemis
summary: Understand schemas, generated operations, caching, and partial failures.
steps: Write a query, mutation, and variables against a small schema.
Compare Ferry and Artemis support, code generation, and maintenance.
Handle partial errors, pagination, and cache updates.
proof: Explain when GraphQL improves a Flutter feature over an existing REST API.

title: WebSocket & Socket.IO
summary: Reconnect, authenticate, order, and reconcile live updates.
steps: Distinguish raw WebSocket from the Socket.IO protocol.
Implement reconnect/backoff and subscription cleanup.
Reconcile missed or duplicate events with a durable source of truth.
proof: Recover a live screen after a network drop without duplicate records.

title: Firebase, Supabase & Appwrite
summary: Compare auth, database, storage, and functions against the same product requirements.
steps: Compare the three platforms’ data models, access rules, and deployment model.
Build one authenticated CRUD/storage flow in a chosen platform.
Document permissions, usage limits, portability, and backup options.
proof: Justify one platform choice and demonstrate blocked cross-user access.

title: gRPC & Protocol Buffers
summary: Typed contracts, code generation, streaming, and compatibility.
steps: Define a small protobuf service and generate Dart bindings.
Handle status codes, deadlines, cancellation, and authentication.
Compare mobile transport with browser/gRPC-Web constraints.
proof: Explain where gRPC fits and evolve a message without breaking clients.

title: MongoDB alongside PostgreSQL
summary: Compare document and relational models using real access patterns.
steps: Model the same feature as relational tables and MongoDB documents.
Compare embedding, references, indexes, consistency, and migrations.
Keep database credentials on a backend and benchmark a representative query.
proof: Choose a data model from requirements rather than framework familiarity.

title: Golden tests & visual regression
summary: Make important visual expectations repeatable without brittle snapshots everywhere.
steps: Create a focused golden test for a stable component.
Control fonts, theme, size, locale, and test environment.
Review changes and combine visual checks with behavior tests.
proof: Catch a deliberate visual regression and explain legitimate golden updates.

title: Flavors & environment configuration
summary: Separate development, staging, and production builds safely.
steps: Configure application IDs, names, icons, and endpoints per environment.
Keep secrets out of compiled Dart values and source control.
Build and verify each flavor in CI.
proof: Install staging and production side by side and identify their backend connections.

title: Shorebird & patch delivery
summary: Understand what a code patch can change and how to release and recover it safely.
steps: Evaluate supported targets, update limitations, and current store requirements.
Practice release, patch, staged rollout, and recovery in a test app.
Track patch versions alongside crash and performance reports.
proof: Explain when a patch is suitable and when a full store release is required.

title: Biometric authentication
summary: Use local device verification alongside secure sessions and server authorization.
steps: Integrate local_auth with fallback and cancellation states.
Distinguish device verification from server identity/authorization.
Test unavailable biometrics, enrollment changes, and a locked device.
proof: Protect a local action without treating biometrics as a server-issued login token.

title: On-device ML: LiteRT & ONNX
summary: Compare local inference with hosted AI APIs using quality, privacy, latency, and device cost.
steps: Run a small TensorFlow Lite/LiteRT or ONNX model on a target device.
Match preprocessing, tensor shapes, quantization, and postprocessing.
Compare latency, memory, battery, quality, and a hosted fallback.
proof: Ship one measured inference flow with appropriate data handling and fallback.

title: Flutter Web, Desktop & Wasm
summary: Ship across platforms with deliberate renderer, compiler, input, and plugin decisions.
steps: Build a desktop target and a Flutter web target, including Wasm where compatible.
Audit plugin support, JS interop, file access, keyboard input, and accessibility.
Measure startup, bundle size, rendering, and distribution requirements.
proof: Document platform differences and ship the same feature with appropriate behavior.

title: Dart FFI & native libraries
summary: Integrate a small C/C++ library with explicit ownership and ABI boundaries.
steps: Bind a small native function and define its supported targets.
Handle pointer lifetime, allocation, strings, and errors.
Measure call overhead and move blocking work off the UI path.
proof: Call native code safely and explain when FFI is better suited than platform channels.

title: Embedded Dart & edge devices
summary: Explore Raspberry Pi, IoT, offline operation, and device-specific runtimes.
steps: Check OS/CPU/runtime/embedder support for the chosen device.
Build a small local sensor or inference prototype.
Test startup, intermittent connectivity, updates, and resource limits.
proof: Explain runtime support and operate a small device prototype reliably.

title: ARKit & ARCore integration
summary: Explore a small augmented-reality feature and its native-platform constraints.
steps: Compare device support, tracking, anchors, and permissions.
Prototype a single AR interaction through a maintained integration or native code.
Test interruption, tracking loss, thermal limits, and accessibility fallback.
proof: Demonstrate a constrained AR feature and explain its platform limits.

title: Rive, Lottie & Flame
summary: Choose interactive animation, playback, or game tooling for a concrete use case.
steps: Compare Rive state machines, Lottie animation playback, and Flame game loops.
Build one small interaction using the appropriate tool.
Measure asset size, frame cost, input behavior, and reduced-motion fallback.
proof: Explain why the chosen tool fits and ship a measured prototype.

title: WalletConnect & Ethers.dart
summary: Explore wallet connections, signing, chain state, and transaction UX on a test network.
steps: Review WalletConnect/Reown and the current Ethers.dart client’s compatibility.
Connect a test wallet and distinguish a message signature from a transaction.
Handle chain/account changes, rejection, and pending/failed transactions.
proof: Explain the trust boundaries and demonstrate a test-network-only interaction.
